name: Antidepressants / anxiety meds

card.summary: Rx mental-health drugs used for anxiety and depression; not appearance treatments, with modest effects and real side effects.
card.note: FDA warning on suicidality in young people; discontinuation symptoms reported.

quick.overview:
Antidepressants are prescription drugs for depression and anxiety disorders. In looksmaxxing they appear as a medication option for appearance-related distress.

They are not appearance treatments, and no study tests them for that.
quick.mechanism: Most block reuptake of serotonin, sometimes with norepinephrine, raising signaling in the brain.
quick.risks: Reported effects include sexual dysfunction, weight change and emotional blunting. An FDA warning covers suicidal thinking in under-25s, and stopping suddenly can cause discontinuation symptoms. Prescription only.

lead: Antidepressants and anxiety medications are prescription drugs used for depression, anxiety disorders, OCD and PTSD. They are not cosmetic treatments, but in looksmaxxing communities they come up because mood and anxiety shape how a person looks and presents: energy for training and grooming, willingness to go out and be seen, posture, eye contact and ease in conversation. Forum members discuss them as a way to lower the social anxiety or low mood that can undercut an otherwise improved appearance.[1][12]

The main classes are SSRIs, SNRIs, tricyclics and MAOIs. Meta-analyses find they outperform placebo in depression by a modest margin; for anxiety disorders the drug-placebo effect size is about 0.3.[1] A 2023 umbrella review of antidepressant trials in people with depression alongside medical illness reported small to medium effect sizes.[2]

Looksmaxxing threads also raise appearance-related questions about the drugs themselves, such as whether they affect skin, collagen, testosterone or weight. A 2025 network meta-analysis ranked individual antidepressants on physiological changes including weight, blood pressure and lab values.[3] Common reported adverse effects include sexual dysfunction, weight change and emotional blunting.[1]

chain: More energy and willingness to train, groom and socialise
Calmer, more open presentation of one's looks
angle.text: People who take these medications for a diagnosed condition often describe being better able to keep up with exercise, skincare, sleep and social life, all of which feed into how they look and come across. Some looksmaxxing forum members also discuss anxiety medication specifically for social confidence.

infobox: SSRIs, SNRIs, TCAs, MAOIs and others

paras: Medical uses include depression, anxiety disorders, chronic pain and some eating disorders.[1] Some drugs hold specific approvals; paroxetine is approved for social anxiety and PTSD.[1] Antidepressants are also studied for neuropathic pain, where an international pain-society review of randomised trials assessed several drug classes.[4]

No trial has tested antidepressants as an appearance treatment. In looksmaxxing forums, users describe them as a route to lower anxiety and improved mood, while other threads collect opinions on anxiety and social-anxiety medications.[12][14]

Effects over placebo are modest, around 30 to 50 percent of people do not respond to a given drug, and critics argue trial design and publication bias inflate benefit.[1] A trial of 141 patients with depression or anxiety disorders compared antidepressants with running therapy under a partially randomised patient-preference design and examined both mental and physical health outcomes.[5] A 2024 network meta-analysis reported that exercise modalities such as walking, jogging, yoga and strength training reduced depression scores compared with active controls.[6] A 2021 trial examined maintaining versus discontinuing antidepressants in primary care.[7]

Common effects include dry mouth, weight changes, dizziness, headaches, akathisia, sexual dysfunction and emotional blunting.[1] A 2025 network meta-analysis compared antidepressants against placebo on weight, cholesterol, glucose, heart rate, blood pressure and other measures, finding differences between individual drugs.[3] A systematic review also catalogued oral manifestations such as dry mouth in people on these drugs.[8]

An FDA warning describes increased suicidal thinking and behavior in children, adolescents and young adults, highest in the first one to two months.[1] Roughly 20 to 50 percent who stop suddenly report discontinuation symptoms.[1]

On looksmax.org, discussion ranges from people asking about prescriptions for anxiety to threads on keeping testosterone up while taking them.[13] Some posters describe starting or stopping specific drugs and the effects they noticed.[15][16] On T Nation, members mention antidepressants such as mirtazapine alongside testosterone therapy and treat low testosterone and depression as separate matters.[17] Hacker News threads debate whether antidepressants are over-prescribed while still helping some patients.[18]

No studies found for looks-related anxiety or appearance outcomes. Trials of the drug class address general conditions: an antidepressant safety study in young people with anxiety, depressive and obsessive-compulsive disorders (n=569),[9] and a trial comparing sertraline with virtual-reality exposure for social anxiety disorder.[10] A 2023 meta-analysis of maintenance-phase treatment compared relapse rates between antidepressants.[11]

lore.intro: Looksmax.org members discuss antidepressants and anxiety medication as tools for mood and social confidence, and with questions about side effects on skin, hormones and weight.[12][13]

claims.claim: Antidepressants might damage collagen or age the skin
claims.believers: Forum posters have asked whether the drugs could harm collagen or age the skin, usually in the context of skin concerns.
claims.experts: No published studies found in this material examine antidepressants and skin collagen; reviews of side effects list metabolic, cardiovascular and oral effects.[3][8]

claims.claim: Antidepressants lower testosterone, so levels must be actively maintained
claims.believers: A thread asks how to maintain testosterone while on most antidepressants, reflecting a belief that the drugs suppress it.[13]
claims.experts: The trials listed here do not report on testosterone; their documented adverse effects include sexual dysfunction.[1]

claims.claim: Anxiety medication helps with social confidence
claims.believers: Threads on best social-anxiety medications and eager posts about starting a prescription show members seeing medication as a way to feel more at ease around others.[14][15]
claims.experts: Paroxetine holds an approval for social anxiety, and a registered trial is comparing sertraline with virtual-reality exposure for it.[1][10]

claims.claim: Antidepressants dull feelings rather than improve mood
claims.believers: Some forum posters say the drugs do not make people happier but only blunt distress, a view that echoes the emotional blunting listed among reported side effects.[1]
claims.experts: Meta-analyses report modest benefit over placebo in depression, with emotional blunting listed among reported adverse effects.[1][2]
